title: Kellton Tech Solutions Ltd - 519602 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Kellton Q1 FY27 revenue about INR 316 crore (near 7% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.1%, PAT INR 22.3 crore; management declined multi-year guidance.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about INR 316 crore, close to 7% YoY growth, with EBITDA of INR 35 crore (11.1% margin) and PAT of INR 22.3 crore (7.1% margin), EPS 42 paise. Operational highlights included completion of an Optima deployment for Oil India across 46 sites and 80-odd wells in under six months, plus several new client wins across the US, UAE and Middle East. Management said the FCCB round was delayed due to market headwinds, and that US client contract starts were being pushed out amid renewed geopolitical conflict. Management declined to give multi-year guidance, citing global uncertainty, and said it expects to meet or beat the FY27 outlook based on a nine-month order book.

financial_highlights.change: stated as up, no base given
management said broadly flat as a percentage, absolute receivables rising

financial_highlights.value: about INR 4 crore in the quarter

segments.name: Oil & Gas / Industrial IoT (Optima)
segments.commentary: Optima deployment for Oil India completed in under six months across 46 sites and 80-odd wells in the Northeast, adding sensors and production intelligence.

segments.name: Middle East / GCC
segments.commentary: Strategic JV with an energy company targets 5% of a USD 1 billion market (oil and gas); Kuwait is the first next step beyond the UAE.

segments.name: Kumori (ServiceNow)
segments.commentary: Acquired for ServiceNow capability rather than revenue; contributed about INR 4 crore in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: No multi-year (two-year or longer) guidance given; management cited geopolitical, AI-driven and macro uncertainty.
Management said it expects to meet or beat the FY27 outlook, citing a predictable order book for the next nine months.
Management declined to commit to a specific growth band (10-20% was floated by an analyst) for FY27.
capex_capacity: Optima oil-field deployment for Oil India completed in under six months.
Phoenix.ai modernisation framework: claimed about 80% faster legacy modernisation at roughly half the cost; a current project covers about 4 million lines of code.
Structi.ai AI context engine launched; claimed to process millions of assets across formats.
demand_pricing: Client wins included a Fortune India 500 conglomerate, a UAE group (cloud-native operating system), a Middle East energy infrastructure company, an industrial services firm, a pest-management leader, an agriculture company and an NBFC (loan origination modernisation enabling a loan-against-property product).
Management said delayed contract starts are rising because clients are worried about their own cash flow after the war restarted.
Management said AI is now a component of almost every project; pure AI projects are small. Claimed about 30% delivery efficiency from internal KAI platform.
Snowflake select-tier partnership achieved during the quarter.
Government of Karnataka HRMS2 program (about 55 departments, 5 lakh+ employees) won a BW gold award for HR tech implementation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Kumori acquisition and the status of the INR 50 crore FCCB fundraising?
qa_highlights.answer: Kumori was bought for ServiceNow capability and certifications, not revenue; it contributed about INR 4 crore this quarter. The FCCB round has been done in part but delayed due to headwinds, and management said it is a matter of time.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and is there a provisioning risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DSO is 100+ days, driven by Fortune 100 US clients on 90-day terms and Indian government and LIC customers with long payment cycles. Write-offs are only a handful of crore over a period of about a year, mainly for uncollectible or disputed amounts; percentage terms are broadly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of delayed contract starts or weaker demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are being signed but starts are delayed as clients worry about cash flow; demand itself is not the issue. Management expects the business to be at par or better than its plan.

qa_highlights.question: Can management provide two-year or longer guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said no one can give multi-year guidance given geopolitical and AI-driven change, and pointed to one-year guidance practice across large companies.

qa_highlights.question: How does AI strategy differentiate and generate revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it uses its internal KAI platform for about 30% delivery efficiency and sells Phoenix.ai and Structi.ai externally, with a campaign targeting legacy modernisation where it claims about 50% cost savings versus competitors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for the GCC energy JV beyond the immediate opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GCC is new to Kellton, so a local partner was needed; the target is 5% of a USD 1 billion oil and gas market, expanding beyond the UAE with Kuwait as the next step.

risks_watch: DSO above 100 days and rising absolute receivables; watch for provisions or write-offs beyond the handful of crore cited.
FCCB fundraise delayed; watch for completion timing and terms.
Delayed US client contract starts linked to geopolitical conflict and client cash-flow concerns.
No multi-year guidance; visibility limited to roughly nine months of order book.
Kumori contribution small (about INR 4 crore per quarter), so the acquisition is not yet revenue-accretive.
summary.management_tone: Confident on product and client wins, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined multi-year guidance and deferred the FCCB timing to market headwinds.
key_quotes: We have achieved INR 316 crores, which is about close to 7% year-on-year growth with an EBITDA of 11.1%
There's no, nobody can give that guidance at this point because of the changes that are happening around the world.

growth.why: Management declined multi-year and numeric FY27 guidance, saying it expects to meet or beat FY27 outlook on a nine-month order book, while US contract starts are being delayed; no capacity additions were disclosed.
